source: 오픽 답변 에피소드 (스픽 저장 문장 활용) 문서, 2026-11-16

question.en: Let's start the interview now. Tell me something about yourself.
question.ko: 이제 인터뷰를 시작하겠습니다. 자신에 대해 말해 주세요.

lines.en: Hi, my name is Jinwoo Oh.
I work for Hanwha Ocean, and right now I'm based at our shipyard in Philadelphia.
lines.ko: 저는 한화오션에서 일하고 있고, 지금은 필라델피아에 있는 저희 조선소에서 근무합니다.

lines.en: I recently took on a new project.
We're expanding the shipyard.
I mainly manage contracts.
I also keep track of progress and risks.
To be honest, I have a lot on my plate these days.
lines.ko: 솔직히 요즘은 할 일이 너무 많아요.

lines.en: Everything is new, the people, the rules, even the way meetings run.
lines.ko: 사람도, 규칙도, 회의하는 방식까지 다 새롭거든요.

lines.en: But I'm slowly getting the hang of it.
I live in Bala Cynwyd with my family, just outside the city.
lines.ko: 저는 도심 바로 밖 발라신윈드에서 가족과 함께 살고 있습니다.

lines.en: On weekends I try to take it easy and spend time with them.
lines.ko: 주말에는 쉬엄쉬엄 가족과 시간을 보내려고 합니다.

lines.en: That's a little bit about me.

question.en: Tell me about the place where you live. What does your home look like?
question.ko: 사는 곳에 대해 말해 주세요. 집은 어떻게 생겼나요?

lines.en: I live in an apartment in Bala Cynwyd, a quiet town right outside Philadelphia.
lines.ko: 저는 필라델피아 바로 옆의 조용한 동네인 발라신윈드의 아파트에 살고 있습니다.

lines.en: We moved in this May, so it still feels pretty new.
lines.ko: 올해 5월에 이사해서 아직도 꽤 새집 같아요.

lines.en: It's a newer building, so everything is clean and bright.
lines.ko: 지은 지 얼마 안 된 건물이라 전부 깨끗하고 밝습니다.

lines.en: When we first moved in, we bought a big desk for the living room.
lines.ko: 처음 이사 왔을 때 거실에 둘 큰 책상을 샀어요.

lines.en: But honestly, the new desk takes up too much space in the room.
lines.ko: 그런데 솔직히 새 책상이 방에서 너무 많은 공간을 차지해요.

lines.en: So I think we need to get rid of some furniture.
lines.ko: 그래서 가구를 좀 치워야 할 것 같아요.

lines.en: The best part is the neighborhood.
There are lots of trees, and in the fall the colors are amazing.
lines.ko: 나무가 많아서 가을이면 색깔이 정말 멋져요.

lines.en: I still can't get over this view.
Commuting to work takes up a lot of time in the morning.
lines.ko: 아침에 출근하는 데 시간이 꽤 걸려요.

lines.en: But I don't mind, because coming home to this place feels great.
lines.ko: 하지만 이런 집으로 돌아오는 게 좋아서 괜찮습니다.

question.en: Describe a typical day at work. What do you usually do?
question.ko: 평소 회사에서의 하루를 설명해 주세요. 보통 무엇을 하나요?

lines.en: My day starts early.
When I get to the office, I have a lot of emails to catch up on.
That's because the head office in Korea works while we sleep.
lines.ko: 우리가 자는 동안 한국 본사가 일하기 때문이죠.

lines.en: Honestly, reading emails makes up most of my morning.
lines.ko: 솔직히 이메일 읽는 게 아침 시간의 대부분을 차지합니다.

lines.en: After that, I check what's on the schedule for this week.
Then I sync up with my team.
I need to stay on top of the project schedule.
lines.ko: 프로젝트 일정을 놓치지 않고 파악해야 해요.

lines.en: So I compare the plan with the actual progress every day.
lines.ko: 그래서 매일 계획과 실제 진행을 비교합니다.

lines.en: If something is running behind schedule, I flag it early and look into the issue.
lines.ko: 뭔가 일정보다 늦어지면 일찍 알리고 문제를 살펴봅니다.

lines.en: In the afternoon, I usually have meetings with our partners.
I normally get off work around seven.
It's a long day, but I like that every day is different.
lines.ko: 긴 하루지만 매일이 다르다는 점이 좋습니다.

question.en: Tell me about a problem you had at work. What happened, and how did you solve it?
question.ko: 회사에서 겪었던 문제에 대해 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 어떻게 해결했나요?

lines.en: A few months ago, we ran into some issues with the vendor.
lines.ko: 몇 달 전에 공급업체와 문제가 좀 있었습니다.

lines.en: Their drawings kept coming in late.
We were running a couple of weeks behind schedule.
My boss was not happy with it, of course.
lines.ko: 당연히 상사도 마음에 들어 하지 않았죠.

lines.en: First, I looked into the issue to identify the root cause.
lines.ko: 먼저 근본 원인을 찾기 위해 문제를 살펴봤습니다.

lines.en: It turned out the vendor simply had too much on their plate.
lines.ko: 알고 보니 그 업체가 맡은 일이 너무 많았던 거예요.

lines.en: So I set up a meeting, and we ironed out the details.
In the end, we met halfway by splitting the work into two parts.
lines.ko: 결국 작업을 두 부분으로 나누는 선에서 절충했어요.

lines.en: To avoid any delays, we also agreed to touch base every week.
lines.ko: 지연을 막기 위해 매주 확인차 연락하기로도 했습니다.

lines.en: Now we're back on track.
There were some takeaways along the way.
The biggest one is to flag problems sooner.
lines.ko: 가장 큰 건 문제를 더 일찍 알려야 한다는 것입니다.

question.en: Tell me about a memorable meeting you had recently.
question.ko: 최근에 했던 기억에 남는 회의에 대해 말해 주세요.

lines.en: Last month, we had a big meeting with our partner about the schedule.
lines.ko: 지난달에 협력사와 일정에 대해 큰 회의를 했습니다.

lines.en: Before the meeting, I wrote up an agenda.
I asked everyone to review it ahead of time.
I started off with a quick overview of our numbers.
lines.ko: 저는 우리 수치에 대한 짧은 개요로 시작했어요.

lines.en: Then the partner said, "Don't you think the deadline is too tight?"
lines.ko: 그러자 협력사가 "마감이 너무 빠듯하다고 생각하지 않으세요?"라고 했어요.

lines.en: I answered, "That's a valid concern, but I think it's still doable."
lines.ko: 저는 "충분히 우려할 만하지만 여전히 해볼 만하다고 생각합니다"라고 답했습니다.

lines.en: After that, people got a bit sidetracked.
lines.ko: 그 뒤에 이야기가 좀 옆길로 샜어요.

lines.en: So I said, "Let's focus on the issues at hand."
Can we table that topic for the next meeting?
lines.ko: 그 주제는 다음 회의에서 얘기해도 될까요?

lines.en: In the end, we were mostly aligned on the project goals.
lines.ko: 결국 프로젝트 목표에 대해 대부분 의견이 일치했습니다.

lines.en: Before we wrapped up, we went over the next steps.
It was long, but I felt proud of how I handled it.
lines.ko: 길었지만 제가 잘 이끌었다는 생각에 뿌듯했습니다.

question.en: You indicated that you go to the gym. Tell me about your workout routine.
question.ko: 헬스장에 다닌다고 하셨는데요. 운동 루틴에 대해 말해 주세요.

lines.en: I go to a gym near my apartment.
I like working out alone, because I can take it slow and focus on myself.
lines.ko: 혼자 운동하는 걸 좋아하는데, 천천히 제 페이스대로 집중할 수 있기 때문입니다.

lines.en: On weekdays, I block out an hour after work.
lines.ko: 평일에는 퇴근 후 한 시간을 미리 빼 둡니다.

lines.en: On busy days, I just say, "I can squeeze that in today," and do thirty minutes.
lines.ko: 바쁜 날에는 "오늘도 짬을 낼 수 있어"라고 하면서 30분만 합니다.

lines.en: How do I handle stress?
This is the answer.
When work is tough, I tell myself, "Don't let it get you down."
lines.ko: 일이 힘들 때는 "그것 때문에 낙담하지 마"라고 스스로에게 말해요.

lines.en: Then I go lift some weights.
These days, I want to take up golf, too.
A lot of people here play it.
It's a good way to get together with coworkers.

question.en: Tell me about a trip you took recently. Where did you go, and what did you do?
question.ko: 최근에 다녀온 여행에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 가서 무엇을 했나요?

lines.en: This summer, I took a few days off and went to Washington, D.C. with my family.
lines.ko: 이번 여름에 며칠 휴가를 내서 가족과 워싱턴 DC에 다녀왔습니다.

lines.en: It's only a few hours from Philadelphia, so we drove.
lines.ko: 필라델피아에서 몇 시간밖에 안 걸려서 차로 갔어요.

lines.en: There were so many museums and monuments.
It took me hours to take in the sights, but nobody got bored.
lines.ko: 구경하는 데 몇 시간이 걸렸지만 아무도 지루해하지 않았어요.

lines.en: On the second day, we came across a cute café near the National Mall.
lines.ko: 둘째 날에는 내셔널 몰 근처에서 귀여운 카페를 우연히 발견했어요.

lines.en: That turned out to be our favorite spot.
The trip went by too quickly.
I still can't get over how fast time flies.
lines.ko: 시간이 얼마나 빨리 가는지 아직도 믿기지 않아요.

lines.en: Next time, I want to take a week off and go somewhere farther, maybe the Grand Canyon.
lines.ko: 다음에는 일주일 휴가를 내서 그랜드캐니언 같은 더 먼 곳에 가고 싶습니다.

question.en: You want to join a new gym. Call the gym and ask three or four questions.
question.ko: 새 헬스장에 등록하려고 합니다. 헬스장에 전화해서 질문 서너 개를 하세요.

lines.en: Hi, I'm calling about a membership.
I was just wondering.
What kind of plans do you have?
Also, could you walk me through the sign up process?
lines.ko: 그리고 가입 절차를 차근차근 설명해 주실 수 있나요?

lines.en: I'd like to come in this week.
What's your availability on Monday?
And would it be possible to set up a free trial session?
lines.ko: 그리고 무료 체험 수업을 잡아 주실 수 있을까요?

lines.en: One more thing.
I saw a discount on your website.
Does that apply to family members as well?
Could you please let me know by Friday?
Thank you so much.

question.en: You made dinner plans with a friend tonight, but something came up at work. Call your friend, explain the situation, and suggest two or three alternatives.
question.ko: 오늘 밤 친구와 저녁 약속이 있는데 회사에 일이 생겼습니다. 친구에게 전화해서 상황을 설명하고 대안을 두세 개 제시하세요.

lines.en: Hey, it's me.
I'm so sorry, but a problem came up last minute.
My meeting is running over.
And honestly, I have too much on my plate today.
lines.ko: 그리고 솔직히 오늘 할 일이 너무 많아.

lines.en: Sorry, but can I take a rain check?
Let me give you some options.
We could either meet this Friday or have brunch on Saturday.
lines.ko: 이번 금요일에 만나거나 토요일에 브런치를 해도 돼.

lines.en: Or, what if we meet halfway?
I could come to your place after work tomorrow, and we can order chicken.
lines.ko: 내일 퇴근하고 내가 너희 집으로 가서 치킨 시켜 먹어도 되고.

lines.en: Are you down for some chicken and beer?
I feel really bad about this.
I'll make it up to you, I promise.
Just ping me when you're free.
lines.ko: 시간 될 때 그냥 메시지 하나 보내줘.

question.en: You run into a coworker you haven't seen for a while. Ask three or four questions about what they've been up to.
question.ko: 오랫동안 못 본 동료를 우연히 만났습니다. 요즘 어떻게 지냈는지 질문 서너 개를 하세요.

lines.en: Hey, long time no see!
How 'bout we grab some coffee and chat a bit?
lines.ko: 커피 한잔 하면서 얘기 좀 할까요?

lines.en: I have a few minutes before my next meeting.
So, what's been on your plate recently?
I heard your team is really busy these days.
Oh, and how was that conference you told me about?
Did you learn anything useful there?
lines.ko: 거기서 쓸 만한 걸 좀 배우셨어요?

lines.en: Also, you look a little tired today.
What's been on your mind all morning?
As for me, I'm doing well.
Last weekend, I took my family on a picnic, so I feel pretty good.
lines.ko: 지난 주말에 가족을 데리고 소풍을 다녀와서 기분이 꽤 좋아요.

lines.en: Anyway, just ping me when you're free.
lines.ko: 아무튼 시간 될 때 메시지 주세요.

lines.en: Let's grab lunch sometime.

question.en: Your manager asked you to pass along some news to a coworker. Call your coworker and give them the message.
question.ko: 매니저가 동료에게 소식을 전해 달라고 했습니다. 동료에게 전화해서 메시지를 전하세요.

lines.en: Hi Mike, it's Jinwoo.
Sorry to bother you, but I have a couple of messages for you.
lines.ko: 방해해서 미안한데, 몇 가지 전할 말이 있어요.

lines.en: First, Kelly told me to tell you to come in early tomorrow.
lines.ko: 먼저 Kelly가 저한테 내일 일찍 출근하시라고 전해달래요.

lines.en: We have a site inspection at eight, and she wants you there.
Also, it's about the dinner with the vendor tonight.
lines.ko: 그리고 오늘 밤 공급업체와의 저녁 식사 건인데요.

lines.en: Bob told me to tell you to put it on the company card.
lines.ko: Bob이 저한테 비용을 회사 카드로 처리하시라고 전해달래요.

lines.en: Just keep the receipt.
Oh, and one more thing.
Have you heard Audrey is getting promoted?
She's going to lead the planning team starting next month.
Let's take her out for lunch sometime.
Anyway, just ping me when you're free.
lines.ko: 아무튼 시간 될 때 메시지 주세요.

lines.en: I'd like to start off with a quick overview.
Let me check on that.
I didn't quite catch that last part.
I see where you're coming from.
That's a valid point, but I think it's still doable.
At this point, ...
At the end of the day, ...
In a nutshell, ...
There were some takeaways along the way.
That's all from my end.
